what: RED/GREEN proof that the new wiring test actually detects the defect it exists for. A wiring test that passes with the wiring removed proves nothing (class C13).
defect_under_test: train_flagship4b's --v2-cache branch reaching tanitad.data.v2_dataset.build_v2_providers with no parity check at all, on a cache that references no registered corpus key, under --require-parity
procedure: 1. RED: in stack/scripts/train_flagship4b.py replace the `v2_parity = parity.assert_v2_parity_cache(args.v2_cache, label='v2-cache', require=args.require_parity)` call with `v2_parity = None` (i.e. exactly the pre-2026-07-27 state of that branch, which carried no check).
3. GREEN: restore the call verbatim; re-run the same command.

red.failure_line: scripts/train_flagship4b.py:407: in train -> providers = build_v2_providers(args.v2_cache, lru_size=args.v2_lru)
red.assertion: AssertionError: build_v2_providers was REACHED despite an unregistered cache under --require-parity
red.reading: the loader IS reached with the guard removed -- i.e. the escalated finding reproduces on this repo at HEAD, and the test is bound to the real call site, not to a stub.

green.reading: with the guard restored the same cache is refused BEFORE the loader is reached (reached['loader'] is False is asserted, not inferred).

what_this_does_NOT_prove: that the refusal message is the RIGHT one -- that is asserted separately ('unregistered v2 cache' + 'register_v2_sibling.py' must both appear), because a guard that fires for the wrong cause is the same defect one layer down;
anything about the raw --cache-dirs branch, which already had a guard and was not touched except to thread the new opt-in --require-parity through it (default False).
